map.materials: Lambert, vertex-coloured, one building colour; unlit flat ground; unlit path and road ribbons (foot 1.6m, service 3.6m, road 7m).

lights.hemisphere: 0xffffff sky, ground tinted 18% toward palette ground, 0.72

map.wallFootDarkening: Bottom 6m of each wall darkens to 0.7 and grades to full.
map.tallCity: Off-campus towers over 45m turn 30% opaque only while occluding the selection or you-are-here.
map.selectedTint: Selected building lerps 22% toward the accent.
map.floorBand: Solid accent band one storey tall, 0.6m outside the walls, inset 0.1m top and bottom.
map.fog: Ground colour, near 0.9x and far 1.55x camera distance.
map.camera: FOV 40; overview tilt 0.9 rad from straight down with Taft Avenue at the bottom; building tilt 1.02 rad.

components.name: Search Pill

components.html: Beta

narrative.northStar: The Architect's Model in a Familiar Map
narrative.overview:
The interface is the map app every student already knows: a full-screen map, a floating search pill on top, one bottom sheet, round map buttons. It is executed straight, in the phone's own system face, with white floating chrome on soft shadows. Nothing in the chrome needs learning. Under it sits something no other map of the campus has: a pale massing model of DLSU Manila, every building one colour and shaped by light alone, on a flat saturated ground with thin bright paths, the city around it muted so the campus leads.

Colour does one job. A single fixed green marks the selection, the found floor, "you are here" and the one primary action, in both themes and on every map palette. Everything else is green-tinted neutral. Density is a phone map's density: one primary action per sheet, rows at least 56px tall, groups made by spacing and type weight rather than boxes. The signature is the found floor drawn as a solid green band one storey tall around the building, with a floor chip beside it.

The map palette is still open (D13 options A orange, B green, C grey); the prototype ships A as the default and a switcher in the info sheet to compare them on phones. The interface never changes with it.
keyCharacteristics: Google Maps convention, never Google's identity: no Google logo, Google Sans or Google pin.
One interface green (#00703c) on green-tinted neutrals, fixed across themes and map palettes.
White floating chrome with soft, low shadows; flat surfaces inside the sheet.
D13 massing model: one pale building colour, unlit flat ground, thin bright paths, soft wall-foot darkening.
Signature: the found floor as a solid accent band one storey tall, plus a floor chip.
Motion confirms: a 260ms sheet snap and 650ms camera flights, both cuts under reduced motion.

rules.name: The One Green Rule
rules.body: Campus Green means "this is yours": the selection, its floor, where you are, the next step. It never decorates, and no map palette may change it or add a second accent.

rules.name: The Fill-Versus-Ink Rule
rules.body: Green fills stay `accent` in both themes; green text and strokes switch to `accent-ink-dark` on dark surfaces. Never put `accent` text on a dark surface.

rules.name: The Two Worlds Rule
rules.body: Interface colours live in CSS tokens; map colours live in the palette table. The interface never samples the map palette, and the map never uses interface neutrals except the accent.

rules.name: The Code Is the Headline Rule
rules.body: On a room card the code is the largest thing on screen and the floor words are the only green text. Building and floor arrive before anything else.

rules.name: The Tabular Code Rule
rules.body: Any room code or floor number sits in tabular figures so codes line up in lists.

rules.name: The Sixteen Floor Rule
rules.body: PRODUCT.md sets 16px as the text floor. The 12–14px roles above shipped in the prototype and are open against that floor; do not add new roles below 16px, and reconcile the existing ones before the real app.

rules.name: The Float-Only-Chrome Rule
rules.body: Shadows belong to things floating over the map. Inside the sheet, use space and weight, not shadowed cards.

rules.name: The Shaped-by-Light Rule
rules.body: Map buildings get one colour and the lights. No outlines, windows, textures or per-building colours; the only exception is the selected building's 22% tint toward the accent.

dos: Do keep exactly one primary button per sheet, Campus Green, full width, 52px.
Do use `accent` for green fills in both themes and `accent-ink-dark` for green text on dark surfaces.
Do put every map label on a surface plate with the Float shadow, so text reads on any ground colour.
Do frame selections in the uncovered map area and fly to a heading that sees the floor band.
Do show the building and floor first on any room result; the route comes after.
Do keep tap targets at 48px for icon and map buttons and 56px for rows.
Do cut every transition and camera flight under `prefers-reduced-motion`.
Do keep "Map data © OpenStreetMap contributors" visible on the map and the Beta tag in the pill.
donts: Don't use Google's identity: no Google logo, Google Sans or Google map pin.
Don't use DLSU's seal, logo or official marks; the green is a colour, not a mark.
Don't add a second accent, or let a map palette change the interface green.
Don't give map buildings outlines, windows, textures or individual colours; light and the selection tint only.
Don't wrap sheet content in shadowed cards or add dividers between rows; group with spacing and weight.
Don't add entrance animations or motion that delays reading.

Don't copy prototype-only scaffolding into the real app: three.js r147 and its OrbitControls from a CDN (the app self-hosts React Three Fiber and works offline), the sample rooms and their "Sample room" marker, the D13 palette switcher (remove once the palette is decided), the "Prototype:" notes and the Start toast, and the label-collision width estimate.
Don't add new text roles below 16px or tap targets below 48px (chips and the secondary button at 44px and segments at 40px are open against PRODUCT.md's floor).
